drafts.draft_en: Thriller (1958). What if the King of Pop dropped it in the black-and-white era? Every frame AI, grain and gate weave included. Saturday Challenge: pick a song, pick a decade, post yours below 👇
drafts.video_tip: 12-15s, 4:3 black and white, heavy grain, slight gate weave, a 1950s soundstage with a crooner band. 3 cuts on the beat, end on a title card 'THRILLER (1958)'. Drop the prompt in the first reply.

drafts.draft_en: I gave myself 60 seconds of render time with Pika H3 Flex. Here's the VFX shot I got. The speed is real, but the trick is the reference frame. Breakdown below 👇
drafts.video_tip: Split screen: left a timer counting to 0:07, right the finished 15s VFX shot (portal opening in a Marseille street). Then a 3s cut to the single reference frame you used.

drafts.draft_en:
Prompt share: VFX creature reveal 🎬

A [creature] emerging from [environment] at [time of day], practical-effects look, [lens]mm anamorphic, volumetric [light color] backlight, debris and dust in the air, cinematic slow push-in. Swap the brackets and post yours.
drafts.video_tip: 4-image grid of the same template with 4 swaps (kraken in the Old Port, golem in a desert, dragon in fog, ghost in a hallway), then a 5s animated version of the best one.

drafts.draft_en: A Halloween horror film that never existed (1979). Made with AI, from storyboard to final grade. The prompt is below if you want to try it before tomorrow night 🎃
drafts.video_tip: 20s fake trailer: faded 70s stock, VHS title font, 4 shots (empty fairground, mask in a window, flashlight in the woods, scream cut to black). Post the full prompt in reply 1.

drafts.draft_en: People still say AI isn't ready for real VFX work. This shot took me one afternoon. Same shot, traditional pipeline: about two weeks. Before/after below.
drafts.video_tip: Wipe transition from the raw plate to the final AI VFX composite, 8-10s, with a small on-screen timer '1 afternoon vs 2 weeks'. Keep the hook text on screen for the first 2s.
